name: Insomnia Coach
one_liner: Free VA app that walks you through a five-week self-guided CBT for insomnia (CBT-I) plan, with a sleep diary and sleep tools. No account.
best_for: Adults with ongoing trouble falling or staying asleep who want to try CBT-I on their own
Veterans and service members, though anyone can use it
People who want a free, structured sleep program with no ads
People waiting for or not ready for in-person insomnia treatment
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988 (veterans press 1)
People with possible sleep apnea, restless legs or another medical sleep problem, who should see a clinician first
People who want a clinician to guide them (the VA's CBT-i Coach app is made to use alongside therapy)
short_description: A free five-week self-guided CBT-I program from the VA's National Center for PTSD, with a sleep diary, weekly feedback and tools for better sleep.
long_description: Insomnia Coach was made by the VA's National Center for PTSD for veterans, service members and anyone else with insomnia. It is based on cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I), the recommended first treatment for chronic insomnia, delivered as a five-week self-guided plan: you keep a daily sleep diary, get personal feedback on your sleep, and work through tools such as sleep scheduling and relaxation. It is free with no ads and needs no account; VA says it cannot see or store what you enter, which stays on your phone, though the app collects anonymous usage data you can switch off. A 2022 pilot randomized trial in 50 veterans with moderate insomnia found the app feasible and acceptable, with larger improvements in insomnia severity, sleep quality and depression symptoms than a waitlist. It is self-help and does not replace a medical evaluation for other sleep problems.
patient_summary: You follow a five-week plan based on CBT-I: log your sleep each day, get feedback, and try one new sleep tool at a time. It is free from the VA, needs no account, and what you enter stays on your phone. It works on its own or alongside care from a clinician.

pricing.notes: Free from the VA, with no ads or in-app purchases.

privacy.notes: No account; VA says it cannot access, store or share what you enter, which stays on your device. Anonymous usage data is collected for research and can be turned off in Settings; deleting the app removes your entries.

seo.title: Insomnia Coach: Review & Pricing
seo.meta_description: Insomnia Coach is a free five-week self-guided program from the VA, based on cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I).

faqs.q: How much does Insomnia Coach cost?
faqs.a: Free. Prices were checked in October 2026 and can change, so confirm with Insomnia Coach before you sign up.

faqs.q: Can Insomnia Coach replace therapy or treatment?
faqs.a: No. Insomnia Coach is a self-help tool that can support your wellbeing or work alongside therapy, but it doesn't diagnose or treat conditions. If you're in crisis, call or text 988 in the US.

faqs.q: Where can I use Insomnia Coach?
faqs.a: Insomnia Coach is available on iPhone and Android.
Five-week CBT-I training plan; Sleep diary; Personal sleep feedback; 17 sleep tools.

clinical_trials.study: Insomnia Coach vs 6-week waitlist in US veterans with moderate insomnia

citation.authors: Kuhn E, Miller KE, Puran D, Wielgosz J, YorkWilliams SL, Owen JE, Jaworski BK, Hallenbeck HW, McCaslin SE, et al.
citation.title: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial of the Insomnia Coach Mobile App to Assess Its Feasibility, Acceptability, and Potential Efficacy

clinical_trials.outcome: Feasible and acceptable; app users improved more than waitlist on insomnia severity, sleep onset latency, sleep quality and depression symptoms.

availability.note: Free from the US Department of Veterans Affairs for anyone, on iPhone and Android.
